ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Sustainability
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Sustainability will publish significant original research from a broad range of natural, social and engineering fields about sustainability, its policy dimensions and possible solutions. Understanding how to ensure the well-being of current and future generations within the limits of the natural world is the overarching goal of sustainability research. Nature Sustainability will cover topics including water, air and soil pollution, agriculture and food security, water–energy–land nexus, water-soil-waste nexus and climate change, among many others.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Air filters with sustained breathability
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01943-3

Although essential to protect human health, air purification technologies suffer from clogging, short lifespans and repeated cartridge replacements. A wet-interface filter design now addresses these challenges, enabling efficient capture of airborne pollutants while prolonging filter service time.
ns1:item.dc:title: Air filters with sustained breathability
ns1:item.dc:creator: Xiaoxue Yao
Steven Wang

ns1:item.ns1:title: Highly efficient air purification by a charge-induced liquid-lined filter
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01920-w

High-efficiency air purification conventionally comes at the price of reduced service lifetimes or elevated operating costs. This paper presents a charge-induced liquid-lined filter that achieves ultrahigh efficiency, long-term durability and low maintenance for sustainable air purification.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Green synthesis of hydrogen and formaldehyde from methanol with enhanced quantum efficiency
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01959-9

Catalytic conversion of methanol to hydrogen potentially offers a safer and greener alternative to conventional hydrogen production routes. This Article presents a single-atom-based catalytic cluster that enables efficient hydrogen production from methanol with the co-generation of valuable formaldehyde instead of CO2.
ns1:item.dc:title: Green synthesis of hydrogen and formaldehyde from methanol with enhanced quantum efficiency
